decisions.reason: As a consumer-facing superfood product with comparatively weak fit to the firm's industrial sustainability core, A is the most likely to miss aspirations and be discontinued so resources can be redirected to stronger technology ventures.

B fits the established waste-to-energy business and can be supported as a modular extension, so with industry growth and some organizational slack management would likely keep it unless results clearly disappoint.

C received a dedicated launch and sits squarely in the firm's core decentralized waste-to-energy offer, making it likely to stay on the market while management continues learning and commercialization.

D is strategically close to the core business and aligned with the firm's waste-to-fuel mission, so despite uncertainty and likely high commercialization demands management would more likely retain it than drop it.
